title: Durable Claude provider-profile content and current resolver
description: OBJECTIVE: remove the root authority gap blocking task-9a1eb61d: current `provider.probe` durably stores only an opaque `providerMinimumProfileRef` plus truth class, project configuration stores seven opaque selection refs, and runtime observation proves the installed binary but contains no selected model, snapshot evidence, effort, or profile revision. CURRENT-BYTE EVIDENCE at HEAD 52584ea7124ebbed56de52963821a78f2a0003d7: production grep finds no `ProviderProfileRevision`, `ProviderCapabilities`, or current profile resolver. DELIVERABLE: a daemon-owned, versioned/content-addressed Claude provider-profile body admitted only inside the authenticated ADMIN `provider.probe` observation, persisted canonically with the probe, and a read-only `resolveCurrentProviderProfile` that returns `ProviderCapabilities` only after binding the profile to the exact current project configuration, probe, and ProjectActivated witness. The profile is operator-configured durable authority, not a host observation and never a dispatch-request field. Exact body: provider literal; distinct `providerMinimumProfileRef` and `profileRevisionId`; all seven project-configuration selection refs; selectedModelId; model snapshot kind/evidence; reasoning effort; adapter capability-schema digest; concurrencyCeiling; and explicit stdout/stderr/tail/timeout values plus their closed mapping to `capturedOutputBytes`,`capturedOutputBytes`,`uiTailBytes`,`runnerAuthorizedMsPerAttempt`. The resolver derives configurationDigest from current settingsDigest, policyDigest from the activation witness, and orchestrationDigest from the current orchestration source SHA. It authenticates origin/currentness but does not declare the numeric limits launchable; parent task-9a1 must pass them through the public @moe/runner validator from task-c8a6c80367ed4a3fb21288e05f0cc6d9. NOT IN SCOPE: launch-template composition, input-manifest work, process launch, runner changes, effect.activate widening, or treating runtime version/closure as model identity. CONSUMER: task-9a1eb61d566e47838c9f79c030da1f70, then task-a9fd91c373c244c78df97945965a8038.
definitionOfDone: A focused daemon module defines closed `moe-provider-profile/1` draft/revision records, exact immutable `ProviderProfileRevision` and `ProviderCapabilities` outputs, descriptor-safe/deep-frozen admission, bounded normalized fields, canonical bytes, and a server-computed `profileDigest`; caller-supplied schema version, canonical bytes, or digest never gains authority.

`provider.probe` accepts exactly an authenticated nested observation of `{providerMinimumProfileRef, profile, truthClass}`, requires the envelope ref to equal the profile body's distinct minimum-profile ref, and persists canonical profile bytes/digest with `ProviderProbed`; identical re-probe is byte-stable/idempotent while the same profile identity with different content refuses `PROVIDER_PROFILE_IMMUTABILITY_CONFLICT` at `PROVIDER_PROFILE_REGISTRATION`.

`resolveCurrentProviderProfile(store,{projectId,expectedConfigurationDigest})` captures stable event horizons and returns `ProviderCapabilities` only when all seven profile selection refs exactly equal the current durable configuration, `profileRevisionId` equals current `selection.profileRef`, the probe and ProjectActivated witness name the same `providerMinimumProfileRef`, current settings/policy/orchestration digests are derived from those durable records, configured concurrency/limit values match their named current limit entries, and both probe/activation truth are strong; it never accepts a dispatch override.

Missing, corrupt, stale, cross-project, conflicting, weak-truth, or mismatched evidence returns UNKNOWN with exact stable code and layer: codec `PROVIDER_PROFILE_INPUT_INVALID|VERSION_UNSUPPORTED|NONCANONICAL|DIGEST_MISMATCH` at `PROVIDER_PROFILE_CODEC`; registration `PROVIDER_PROFILE_REF_MISMATCH|IMMUTABILITY_CONFLICT` at `PROVIDER_PROFILE_REGISTRATION`; reader `PROVIDER_PROFILE_ABSENT|UNREADABLE|BINDING_MISMATCH|TRUTH_UNVERIFIED` at `PROVIDER_PROFILE_READER`, preserving upstream store/config code+layer.

Tests use a real file-backed SqliteEventStore and production project.register -> provider.probe, project-configuration selection, and project.activate paths; they include one nonempty accepted control, reopen/byte stability, unchanged event/decision counts on reads, and positive/exact hostile and authoritative-field mutation tables. Separate named mutations bypassing profile/config/probe/activation equality checks must each redden their exact code+layer assertion.

Every production source remains <=250 physical lines (split codec from reader before 400 if measurement requires it), each runtime bridge is exact one-line LF and root-reachable, and standalone @moe/daemon typecheck/test legs record separate exit codes with nonzero Test Files/Tests output; completion records task-9a1eb61d566e47838c9f79c030da1f70 as the real consumer.
taskRails: The only caller-proposed seam is the exact authenticated ADMIN provider.probe profile payload; no dispatch request, optional override, validator-over-request, or runtime observation may supply model, effort, profile, concurrency, or limits.

Keep `providerMinimumProfileRef` distinct from `profileRevisionId`: the former binds probe/activation capability adequacy, the latter binds project configuration `selection.profileRef`; never collapse the two without measured equality.

Runtime observation may bind adapter capability-schema evidence, but reportedVersion, closure digests, or an opaque ref must never be recast as selectedModelId, model snapshot evidence, reasoning effort, or profile revision.
Do not copy private runner ceiling literals or claim limits are launch-admissible; task-c8a6c80367ed4a3fb21288e05f0cc6d9 owns the public runner validator and task-9a1 must compose it.
Fail closed with exact code+layer, assert generated-table cardinality, preserve foreign work, and commit only explicit owned paths.

Final: provider-profile-resolver.ts 181 lines, provider-profile-reader-checks.ts 191 lines, both under 250.
